- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values, especially in early 30d window.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast lows, especially in late 30d window.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 5–7 days, model often lags the sentiment shift; adjust forecast 3–5 days ahead to align with sentiment direction.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 95% of recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +10–15% above recent peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive -1.00), model underestimates; apply upward bias of 2–5% to forecast mean.
- If model forecast mean is consistently higher than true outcome mean over 30d, apply downward correction of 1–3% to forecast, especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) for 5+ days, model tends to drift toward historical mean; use 10-day moving average of past 30d to anchor forecast.
